---
title: "My first weeks in MDS"
author: "Richard von Celsing"
date: 2026-09-10
---
Three weeks ago I moved from the UK to Vancouver to start the Master of Data
Science at UBC. Coming back to full-time study after several years of working
was a strange adjustment. I'd forgotten the rhythm of lectures, labs and
deadlines stacked on top of each other. Orientation and the first week of
classes went by faster than I expected, and it took a while to stop thinking
in terms of project timelines and start thinking in terms of weekly labs.

The pace has been the biggest surprise. I came in expecting the statistics to
be the hard part and the tooling to be familiar, and it's been closer to the
opposite: the volume of new programming tools, languages and tech stacks in
the first few weeks has been relentless. My cohort has made that much easier, and some of
the most useful things I've picked up have come out of working through
problems with the people around me rather than from the lectures themselves.

Three weeks in, I'm tired but genuinely enjoying it. The parts I'm most
looking forward to are still ahead, I want to get into the modelling
courses and start applying this to real problems rather than exercises.
So far my free time has been limited, but I'm hoping to settle in soon and
see more of Vancouver and BC.
